requirements.statement: When the page has a document type declaration, the declaration is placed before the html tag in the source code.

citations.quote: Pour chaque page web possédant une déclaration de type de document, celle-ci est-elle située avant la balise `<html>` dans le code source ?

routes.statement: The DOCTYPE declaration comes before the html tag.

citations.quote: La balise DOCTYPE est placée avant la balise `<html>` ;

rationale.text: The test asks where the declaration sits in the source code. The rendered page does not show that. The HTML parser keeps a DOCTYPE only when it is the first token of the source and drops a misplaced one, so document.doctype is null both for a page with no declaration (to which this test does not apply) and for a page whose declaration follows the html tag (which fails it): a null doctype proves nothing. A doctype present in the DOM proves that one declaration came first, but not that every declaration did: a page assembled from templates can repeat the doctype further down, and the parser drops the second one without trace, although the page then possesses a declaration that is not before the html tag. The shared methodology ("Tests identiques à 8.1.1") also asks that the type be valid, which the DOM cannot fully show either (see 8.1.2). So no check is linked and the entry is none. What would raise it: access to the source as served, tokenized with the HTML standard's tokenizer so that a DOCTYPE inside a comment or a script is not counted; spec section 15 and decision Q9 leave source analysis out of v1. Applicability is judgment: the test applies only to pages that possess a declaration, and the DOM cannot show whether a page possesses a misplaced one. Needs is empty.
